summary.text: Julius Caesar was a Roman general, statesman and author who was dictator of the Roman Republic almost continuously from 49 BC until his assassination in 44 BC.
He led Roman armies through the Gallic Wars, then crossed the Rubicon against the Senate's order in 49 BC and won the civil war that followed.
Senators murdered him fearing he might make himself king, new civil wars followed, and his heir Octavian later turned the Republic into the Roman Empire.

facts.label: First Triumvirate
facts.value: Formed in 60 BC with Crassus and Pompey

facts.label: Assassinated
facts.value: Killed on the Ides of March, 15 March 44 BC

facts.label: Gallic Wars
facts.value: Completed by 51 BC, greatly expanding Roman territory

items.prompt: In early 49 BC the Senate ordered Caesar to give up his command and return to Rome. He crossed the Rubicon with his army instead. What did that act begin?

options.label: A peaceful handover of his army
A new war against the Gauls
A civil war, which he won
A rebellion led by Pompey against him

items.explain: Crossing the Rubicon openly defied the Senate and began Caesar's civil war, which he won.

items.prompt: A group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius plotted against Caesar. What did they fear?

options.label: His domination of the state and a possible bid to be king
His plan to give his power back to Pompey
His string of defeats in foreign wars
His plan to shrink the Senate sharply

items.explain: They feared his power, his domination of the state, and the possibility that he might make himself king.

items.prompt: After Caesar's assassination, what became of the Republic's constitutional government?

options.label: It was restored at once with newly elected consuls
Pompey returned and rebuilt it
The Senate named another dictator for life
New civil wars began and it was never fully restored

items.explain: A new series of civil wars broke out and the constitutional government of the Republic was never fully restored.

items.prompt: After winning the civil war, Caesar carried out reforms. Which was one of them?

options.label: Settling his veterans in new overseas colonies
Cutting the size of the Senate in half
Increasing the size of the grain dole
Restoring the old republican calendar

items.explain: He settled veterans in overseas colonies, greatly increased the Senate, reduced the grain dole and replaced the republican calendar.

items.prompt: The Julii claimed their clan was divine. What was the basis for the claim?

options.label: Descent from a king of Rome who was a son of Mars
The priesthood of Jupiter held by Caesar's father
A gift of land from Tullus Hostilius
Descent from Julus, son of Aeneas, who was a son of Venus

items.explain: The family claimed descent from Julus, son of Aeneas, and since Aeneas was a son of Venus, this made the clan divine.

items.prompt: A trivia buff says Caesar was born by Caesarian section. Why does that claim fail?

options.label: Ancient sources say his mother died in childbirth
Such operations meant the mother's death, but his mother lived for decades
The operation was forbidden by law for patricians
He was born at sea, far from any surgeon

items.explain: There is no evidence for it: such operations entailed the mother's death, yet Caesar's mother lived for decades after his birth.
